title: Problem Overview and References
content: Erdős Problem #800 asks whether graphs with no two adjacent vertices of degree $\geq 3$ have linear Ramsey numbers $R(G) \ll n$. Alon (1994) proved $R(G) \leq 12n$ using the probabilistic method. The header documents the connection to the broader Burr-Erdős conjecture (Problem #163), which was fully resolved by Choongbum Lee in 2016 for all $p$-degenerate graphs.
mathContext: $R(G) \leq 12n$ for graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices with no adjacent vertices of degree $\geq 3$

title: Imports and Namespace
content: Imports Mathlib's simple graph infrastructure (`SimpleGraph.Basic`, `SimpleGraph.Subgraph`, `SimpleGraph.Clique`, `SimpleGraph.Coloring`), finite type machinery, and real number arithmetic for Ramsey bounds. The `open SimpleGraph` brings graph notation into scope. All definitions live in `Erdos800`.
mathContext: Uses `SimpleGraph V` for graphs, `neighborFinset` for degree computation, and $\mathbb{R}$ for Ramsey bound arithmetic

title: Structural Condition: No Adjacent High-Degree Vertices
content: Three definitions build up the key structural condition. `vertexDegree G v` counts $|N(v)|$ using `neighborFinset`. `isHighDegree G v` means $\deg(v) \geq 3$. The central predicate `noAdjacentHighDegree G` states that no edge $uv$ has both $\deg(u) \geq 3$ and $\deg(v) \geq 3$. Equivalently, the set of high-degree vertices forms an independent set. The threshold 3 is natural: degree-2 vertices are exactly the subdivision vertices that separate high-degree vertices in subdivided graphs.
mathContext: $\text{noAdjacentHighDegree}(G) \iff \forall u \sim v,\; \neg(\deg(u) \geq 3 \wedge \deg(v) \geq 3)$; equivalently, the high-degree vertices form an independent set

title: Subdivision Implies No Adjacent High-Degree Vertices (Proved)
content: Defines `isSubdivisionVertex` ($\deg(v) = 2$) and `isOriginalVertex` ($\deg(v) \neq 2$), then proves `subdivision_implies_no_adjacent_high_degree`: if every high-degree vertex's neighbors all have degree $\leq 2$, then no two high-degree vertices are adjacent. The proof is by contradiction with `omega`: if $u \sim v$ and both have degree $\geq 3$, then the hypothesis gives $\deg(v) \leq 2$, contradicting $\deg(v) \geq 3$. This is one of the few fully verified results in the file.

title: Ramsey Number Infrastructure
content: Builds the Ramsey theory framework from scratch. `completeGraph N` defines $K_N$ on `Fin N` with adjacency $u \neq v$. `edgeColoring N` assigns a Boolean (red/blue) to each ordered pair. `isMonochromatic` checks that all edges of an embedded copy of $G$ have the same color. `containsMonochromaticCopy` requires an injective embedding with monochromaticity. The Ramsey number $R(G)$ and its specification are axiomatized — formalizing the finite Ramsey theorem would require substantial combinatorial infrastructure. `hasLinearRamseyNumber G C` means $R(G) \leq C \cdot n$.
mathContext: $R(G) = \min\{N : \forall c\colon E(K_N) \to \{\text{red}, \text{blue}\},\; K_N \text{ contains a monochromatic copy of } G\}$

title: Alon's Theorem (1994): R(G) ≤ 12n
content: The main result, axiomatized as `alon_theorem`: if $G$ on $n$ vertices has no adjacent high-degree vertices, then $R(G) \leq 12n$. Alon's proof uses the probabilistic method. Since the high-degree vertices $H$ form an independent set, they can be randomly embedded into $K_N$. For each high-degree vertex $v$, the paths of degree-2 vertices connecting it to other high-degree vertices can be extended deterministically. The constant $12 = 2 \times 6$ arises from: factor 2 for the two colors in the Ramsey setting, and factor 6 from probabilistic counting of embedding extensions. The corollary `subdivided_graphs_linear_ramsey` chains this with the subdivision theorem.
mathContext: $\text{noAdjacentHighDegree}(G) \Rightarrow R(G) \leq 12|V(G)|$; constant $12 = 2 \times 6$ from color doubling and probabilistic argument

title: Degeneracy and the Burr-Erdős Conjecture
content: Connects Problem #800 to the broader Burr-Erdős conjecture (Problem #163). `isDegenerateAt G p` means every subgraph has a vertex of degree $\leq p$; this is $p$-degeneracy. The axiom `no_adjacent_high_degree_is_2_degenerate` states that graphs with no adjacent high-degree vertices are 2-degenerate. The `burr_erdos_theorem` (Lee 2016) axiomatizes the full conjecture: every $p$-degenerate $n$-vertex graph has $R(G) \leq c_p \cdot n$. The theorem `erdos_800_special_case_of_163` derives Problem #800 as the $p = 2$ case, providing an alternative proof path via the general theorem.
mathContext: $G$ $p$-degenerate $\Rightarrow R(G) \leq c_p n$; graphs with no adjacent high-degree vertices are 2-degenerate, so Problem #800 is the $p = 2$ case

title: Problem Statement and Solution
content: The formal problem statement `erdos800Problem` quantifies over all graphs $G$ with `noAdjacentHighDegree` and asserts existence of a constant $C$ with $R(G) \leq Cn$. The solution `erdos_800` proves this by instantiating $C = 12$ and invoking `alon_theorem`. This is a clean modular proof: unfold `hasLinearRamseyNumber`, then apply the axiomatized bound.
mathContext: $\forall G \text{ with no adjacent high-degree vertices},\; \exists C,\; R(G) \leq C \cdot |V(G)|$; solved with $C = 12$

title: Summary Theorem: Combining Results
content: The `erdos_800_summary` theorem packages two facts as a conjunction: (1) Alon's explicit bound $R(G) \leq 12n$ for all graphs with no adjacent high-degree vertices, and (2) the existential statement `erdos800Problem`. The proof constructs the pair `\langle\lambda\ldots \Rightarrow \text{alon\_theorem},\, \text{erdos\_800}\rangle`. This dual presentation gives both the quantitative bound (constant 12) and the qualitative answer (linear growth exists).
mathContext: $(\forall G,\; R(G) \leq 12n) \wedge (\forall G,\; \exists C,\; R(G) \leq Cn)$
